messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the fairness telemetry sync earlier — I dug into the ingestion gaps we saw in staging and have a few questions.
kevin: thanks — summary?
maria: The core issue looks like high-cardinality tenant tags causing our batch uploader to skip some windows. Specifically when tenant_id + route + model_version exploded for short-lived requests, the aggregator fell back to a 'misc' bucket and we lost weight signals.
nina: ugh, yeah. that misc bucket hides abuse patterns.
devon: do we have a repro? logs or a small script?
maria: repro attached in the gist from staging: https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro-telemetry — shows aggregator flush ignoring >10k keys per minute.
kevin: ok. two angles: 1) reduce cardinality by hashing route/model to a fixed set, 2) increase memory/flow-window on the uploader for a short time. tradeoffs?
nina: hashing reduces signal granularity. for fairness scheduling we need model_version sometimes. but maybe not for long tails.
devon: we could keep full keys in raw event stream (kafka) and only materialize fixed buckets for fast-path admission decisions.
elaine: that seems promising — admission service only needs low-latency, approximate counts. offline jobs can reconstitute per-tenant/model stats for posthoc analysis.
infra-bot: FYI: kafka-topic "telemetry-raw" retention 7d, partitions 12. Current producer backpressure seen at 95th percentile.
maria: proposal: add a light-weight sidecar counter that emits two outputs: (A) fixed-bucket incremental counters every 10s for admission (low latency) (B) full-key events sampled 1% -> raw topic for offline accuracy.
kevin: sampling + fixed buckets should cut ingestion by ~30x. do we lose abuse detection sensitivity with 1%?
nina: depends on the attack mode. high-rate abuse will still surface; long-tail stealthy abuse might not. we could bump sampling to 5% for tenants flagged by heuristics.
devon: how do we flag? maintain a tiny rolling anomaly score in Redis? that adds operational complexity.
elaine: we already have tenant anomaly scores in the risk-service. can emit a sidecar config: if anomaly_score > 0.7 -> sample 5% and forward full keys, else 1%.
maria: ops questions: storage cost for sampled raw events, reprocessing needs, schema stability. infra-bot shows current cost for telemetry S3: $1200/mo for 7d. sampling should keep this flat.
kevin: also need to ensure admission uses monotonic counters (not resets) and supports delta-windowing when the uploader is behind.
nina: can admission tolerate eventual consistency? We have some slack: it's okay to be off by 10-20% for short windows as long as we don't starve tenants.
devon: implementation plan: 1) sidecar counter library (Go) with fixed-bucket hash, sampling policy hook to risk-service, compressed protobuf events -> kafka 2) admission change to read 10s counters and expose per-tenant weight API 3) add dashboards and an alert for "misc-bucket" rate > 1% of ingested keys
maria: timeline?
kevin: spike + prototype in 2 weeks, rollout to staging week after, monitor misc and admission SLOs for 2 weeks, then prod canary.
elaine: operational checklist: migration docs, risk-service contract for sampling config, runbook for disabling sampling (if we need full fidelity), S3 lifecycle policy update.
nina: one more thing: fairness scheduler needs to know when a tenant is in probation. we should add a probation flag to the per-tenant counter payload so admission can short-circuit.
maria: agreed. we'll add a header field: X-Tenant-Probaton:true/false (or JSON field in protobuf) — admission will prefer probation path.
devon: quick snippet for the fixed-bucket hash in Go that I tested:
```go
func bucketKey(tenant, route, model string, buckets int) string {
    h := fnv.New32a()
    h.Write([]byte(route))
    h.Write([]byte(model))
    // keep tenant raw for per-tenant counters
    return fmt.Sprintf("t:%s|b:%d", tenant, int(h.Sum32())%buckets)
}
```
kevin: nice. make sure we document why tenant is raw (we still need per-tenant fairness).
maria: ok I'll write the RFC follow-up with diagrams and the tradeoff table (sampling rate vs detection sensitivity vs cost).
elaine: assign owners?
maria: owner: maria + devon for sidecar lib; kevin + nina for admission changes; infra will support kafka/partition tuning (elaine).
infra-bot: Created task ID TL-7123 for sidecar work; assigned to maria, devon.
maria: thanks — I'll post the RFC link once I draft it. :thumbsup:
kevin: great work everyone. we'll reconvene after the prototype. :calendar:
